```{r setup}
library(data.table)
root <- if (nzchar(params$root)) params$root else normalizePath(".", winslash = "/")
while (!file.exists(file.path(root, "_targets.R")) && dirname(root) != root) root <- dirname(root)
store <- if (nzchar(params$store)) params$store else file.path(root, "_targets_sens")
rd <- function(name) targets::tar_read_raw(name, store = store)
fit <- rd("sens_fit")
st <- rd("sens_table")
cons <- rd("sens_conservative_all")
ld <- rd("sens_limits")
vd <- rd("sens_verdict_table")
cal <- rd("calibration_all")
obs <- rd("obs_all")[[1]]
session <- rd("session")
lab <- setNames(fit$label, fit$dataset)
st[, Model := lab[dataset]]
primary <- st[d_bias_mcse == 0, dataset][1]
vd[, Model := lab[dataset]]
qlab <- c(bias = "Bias correction", ci_lo = "CI: lower limit", ci_hi = "CI: upper limit",
          test_lo = "Test: lower rejection limit", test_hi = "Test: upper rejection limit")
qlow <- c(bias = "bias correction", ci_lo = "lower CI limit", ci_hi = "upper CI limit",
          test_lo = "lower rejection limit", test_hi = "upper rejection limit")
thr <- vd$threshold[1]
# Plain-language verdict per model, from the differences against the primary model
verdict_of <- function(ds) {
  v <- vd[dataset == ds]
  q <- function(st) paste(qlow[v[status == st, quantity]], collapse = ", ")
  if (any(v$status == "relevant")) {
    out <- paste0("practically relevant difference in ", q("relevant"))
  } else if (all(v$status == "negligible")) {
    out <- "no practically relevant difference in any quantity"
  } else {
    out <- "no practically relevant difference shown"
  }
  if (any(v$status == "unclear")) {
    out <- paste0(out, " (not resolved at this precision: ", q("unclear"), ")")
  }
  out
}
bs <- vd[quantity == "bias", status]
ls <- vd[quantity != "bias", status]
answer_bias <- if (any(bs == "relevant")) {
  "At least one model shows a practically relevant difference in the bias correction, so the adjusted point estimate depends on the choice of prediction model."
} else if (all(bs == "negligible")) {
  "The differences in the bias correction are negligible under every model, so the bias correction and the adjusted point estimate are robust to the choice of prediction model."
} else {
  "No model shows a practically relevant difference in the bias correction, but not all differences are resolved at this precision."
}
answer_limits <- if (any(ls == "relevant")) {
  "The CI or rejection limits differ relevantly under at least one model. This changes the width of the adjusted interval and the significance threshold, not the point estimate; the conservative combination in Section 5 protects against it."
} else if (all(ls == "negligible")) {
  "The CI and rejection limits do not differ relevantly either."
} else {
  "For the CI and rejection limits, some differences are not resolved at this precision; the conservative combination in Section 5 covers them."
}
B <- st$n_sim[1]
n0 <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",")
f3 <- function(x) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 3)
f4 <- function(x) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 4)
pct <- function(x, d = 1) paste0(formatC(100 * x, format = "f", digits = d), "%")
pm <- function(x, se, f = f4) paste0(f(x), " (", f(se), ")")
hr <- function(x) formatC(exp(x), format = "f", digits = 3)
fig <- function(path) file.path(root, path)
```

## Summary

The bias correction, the confidence interval and the rejection limits of the QBA are derived from studies simulated under a prediction model fitted to the observed data. Within one model the true value is known, so the adjustment is correct by construction; what can differ between models is the size of the correction that is carried over to the observed estimate. This report repeats the same analysis under three outcome models and compares the results.

- **Design.** Same base data (n = `r n0(nrow(rd("base_all")[[1]]))`), same CCW pipeline and same random numbers under every model: simulated study *b* and large dataset *j* use the same uniform draws under each model. This does not remove Monte Carlo error, but it makes the differences between models much more precise than separate simulations would. `r n0(B)` simulated studies per scenario (calibrated effect and no effect) and model. Simple adjustment only: no nested simulation, no pilot study, hazard ratio endpoint only.
- **Models.** Weibull (primary), exponential (Weibull with the shape fixed at 1) and three-parameter generalized gamma (Weibull at Q = 1), all proportional hazards in the covariates with a time-varying treatment effect.
- **Answer.** `r answer_bias` `r answer_limits` By model: `r paste0(st[dataset != primary, Model], ", ", vapply(st[dataset != primary, dataset], verdict_of, ""), collapse = "; ")`. The threshold for a practically relevant difference is `r f3(thr)` on the log HR scale (5% of the empirical SE of the estimate, `r f3(st[dataset == primary, emp_se])`); a difference counts as negligible or relevant only if it is below or above the threshold by more than twice its Monte Carlo SE, and as not resolved otherwise (Section 4).
- **Largest difference in bias correction from the primary model:** `r f4(st[which.max(abs(d_bias)), d_bias])` on the log HR scale (`r st[which.max(abs(d_bias)), Model]`; MCSE `r f4(st[which.max(abs(d_bias)), d_bias_mcse])`).
- **Adjusted HR:** `r paste0(st$Model, " ", hr(st$est_adj), " (", hr(st$ci_lo_np), " to ", hr(st$ci_hi_np), ")", collapse = "; ")`. Observed HR `r hr(obs$estimate)` (`r hr(obs$ci_lo)` to `r hr(obs$ci_hi)`).

## 1 Prediction models and their fit

```{r tab-fit}
#| tbl-cap: "Fit of the outcome models to the observed data. Likelihood-ratio test with 1 degree of freedom against the Weibull model."
knitr::kable(
  fit[, .(Model = label, Parameters = n_par, `Log-likelihood` = formatC(loglik, format = "f", digits = 2),
          AIC = formatC(aic, format = "f", digits = 1), Shape = shape,
          `Treatment log HR (SE)` = pm(theta_hat, theta_se, f3),
          `LR test p` = ifelse(is.na(lr_p), "", formatC(lr_p, format = "f", digits = 3)))],
  align = "lrrrlrr"
)
```

![Kaplan-Meier curve of the observed outcome (black) and marginal survival implied by each model.](`r fig(rd("fig_sens_fit"))`)

The conservative combination of Section 5 is meant for models that fit about equally well; a model with a clearly worse fit is a stress test of misspecification and should be read as such.

## 2 Calibration and performance of the CCW analysis

```{r tab-cal}
#| tbl-cap: "Inverse calibration (mean simulated estimate = observed estimate) and true value under each model. Log HR scale; Monte Carlo SE in brackets."
cl <- rbindlist(lapply(st$dataset, function(ds) {
  x <- cal[[grep(paste0("(^|_)", ds, "$"), names(cal))[1]]]
  data.table(dataset = ds, steps = x$n_eval, mean_est = x$mean_est, at_bound = x$at_bound)
}))
# Large datasets behind each true value (a failed analysis of a large dataset is left out)
tr <- rd("truth_rows_all")
n_tr <- tr[, .N, by = .(dataset, theta)]
n_max <- max(n_tr$N)
cl <- merge(cl, n_tr[, .(dataset, theta, N)][st[, .(dataset, theta = theta_cal)],
                                               on = .(dataset, theta)][, .(dataset, n_large = N)],
            by = "dataset")
knitr::kable(
  merge(st, cl, by = "dataset", sort = FALSE)[, .(
    Model, `Generating log HR θ*` = f3(theta_cal), `Search steps` = steps,
    `Mean estimate at θ*` = f4(mean_est), `True value ψ(θ*)` = pm(truth, truth_mcse),
    `Large datasets used` = paste(n_large, "of", n_max),
    `Failed simulated studies` = n_fail
  )],
  align = "lrrrrrr"
)
```

```{r truth-fail}
#| results: asis
nf <- n_tr[N < n_max]
if (nrow(nf)) {
  k <- sum(n_max - nf$N)
  where <- paste0(lab[nf$dataset], " model, ",
                  ifelse(abs(nf$theta) < 1e-12, "no effect", "calibrated effect"),
                  " (", n_max - nf$N, " of ", n_max, ")", collapse = "; ")
  cat("The analysis failed in ", k, " large dataset", if (k > 1) "s", ": ", where, ". ",
      if (k > 1) "They were" else "It was",
      " left out of the true values, and the errors are recorded in the pipeline. Failures of this kind come from the survival package (aeqSurv) when a simulated death falls a negligible fraction of a day after a split point, which becomes likely only in datasets of tens of thousands of patients.\n", sep = "")
}
```

```{r tab-perf}
#| tbl-cap: "Performance of the CCW analysis as published (Wald interval, robust SE) under each model. Monte Carlo SE in brackets; the MCSE of the difference from the primary model pairs the simulated studies by replicate and the true values by large dataset."
knitr::kable(
  st[, .(Model, Bias = pm(bias, bias_mcse),
         `Difference from primary` = ifelse(d_bias_mcse == 0, "", pm(d_bias, d_bias_mcse)),
         `Empirical SE` = pm(emp_se, emp_se_mcse), `Model SE` = f4(mod_se),
         `95% CI coverage` = paste0(pct(coverage_wald), " (", pct(coverage_wald_mcse, 2), ")"),
         `Type I error` = paste0(pct(type1_wald), " (", pct(type1_wald_mcse, 2), ")"))],
  align = "lrrrrrr"
)
```

## 3 Adjustment under each model

```{r tab-limits}
#| tbl-cap: "Quantities carried over to the observed analysis. Centred 2.5% and 97.5% quantiles of the simulated estimates at the calibrated effect (CI) and with no effect (rejection limits), log HR scale, Monte Carlo SE in brackets; critical value of |z| for the parametric test."
knitr::kable(
  st[, .(Model, `Bias correction` = pm(bias, bias_mcse),
         `CI: lower` = pm(q_lo, q_lo_mcse, f3), `CI: upper` = pm(q_hi, q_hi_mcse, f3),
         `Test: lower` = pm(null_q_lo, null_q_lo_mcse, f3),
         `Test: upper` = pm(null_q_hi, null_q_hi_mcse, f3),
         `SE inflation` = f3(se_inflation), `Critical |z|` = f3(z_crit_par))],
  align = "lrrrrrrr"
)
```

```{r tab-adj}
#| tbl-cap: "Adjusted analysis of the observed data under each model (hazard ratio scale) and its check in independent simulated studies."
knitr::kable(
  st[, .(Model, `Adjusted HR` = hr(est_adj),
         `95% CI, non-parametric` = paste0(hr(ci_lo_np), " to ", hr(ci_hi_np)),
         `p, non-parametric` = f3(p_np),
         `95% CI, parametric` = paste0(hr(ci_lo_par), " to ", hr(ci_hi_par)),
         `p, parametric` = f3(p_par),
         `Coverage after adjustment` = paste0(pct(coverage_adj), " (", pct(coverage_adj_mcse, 2), ")"),
         `Type I error after adjustment` = paste0(pct(type1_adj), " (", pct(type1_adj_mcse, 2), ")"))],
  align = "lrrrrrrr"
)
```

Coverage and type I error after adjustment are checked within each model, against that model's own true value, in studies that were not used to derive the adjustment. They show that the adjustment works when the model is right, not that it transfers between models; the transfer is what the differences between rows of the tables above describe.

## 4 Is the adjustment robust to the prediction model?

The table compares the quantities that are carried over to the observed analysis with those of the primary model. Simulated studies and large datasets are paired across models (same random numbers), so the Monte Carlo SE refers to the difference itself: for the bias correction it combines the paired simulated studies and the paired true values; for the limits it is a paired bootstrap over simulated studies (`r n0(200)` resamples).

```{r tab-robust}
#| tbl-cap: "Difference from the primary model (log HR scale; limits centred at the mean estimate). Detectable: larger than 2 MCSE. Verdict against the threshold of 5% of the empirical SE: negligible if |difference| + 2 MCSE is below it, relevant if |difference| - 2 MCSE is above it, otherwise not resolved."
knitr::kable(
  vd[, .(Model, Quantity = qlab[quantity], Difference = f4(diff), MCSE = f4(diff_mcse),
         Detectable = ifelse(detectable, "yes", "no"),
         Verdict = ifelse(status == "unclear", "not resolved", status))],
  align = "llrrcc"
)
```

```{r robust-text}
#| results: asis
for (ds in unique(vd$dataset)) {
  cat("- **", lab[[ds]], ":** ", verdict_of(ds), ".\n", sep = "")
}
cat("\n", answer_bias, " ", answer_limits, "\n", sep = "")
```

## 5 Conservative combination across models

Following the draft of Section 3.8: the adjusted estimate closest to no effect, the widest confidence limit and rejection limit on each side, and the largest p-value; the null hypothesis is rejected only if it is rejected under every model. All three models are combined here. If one model fits clearly worse than the others (Section 1), the combination should be restricted to the models with comparable fit.

```{r tab-cons}
#| tbl-cap: "Conservative adjusted analysis across the prediction models."
knitr::kable(
  cons[, .(`Adjusted HR` = hr(est_adj), `95% CI` = paste0(hr(ci_lo_np), " to ", hr(ci_hi_np)),
           `Rejection limits (centred log HR)` = paste0(f3(null_q_lo), " to ", f3(null_q_hi)),
           `Critical |z|` = f3(z_crit_par), `p` = f3(p_np),
           `H0 rejected` = ifelse(reject_np, "yes", "no"))],
  align = "rrrrrr"
)
```

## 6 Run time and software

```{r tab-runtime}
#| tbl-cap: "Computing time by stage and model (sum over targets, all workers)."
meta <- tryCatch(
  as.data.table(targets::tar_meta(fields = c(name, type, seconds), targets_only = TRUE, store = store)),
  error = function(e) NULL
)
if (!is.null(meta) && nrow(meta)) {
  meta <- meta[type %in% c("stem", "branch") & !is.na(seconds)]
  meta[, stage := fcase(
    grepl("^calibration_", name), "Inverse calibration",
    grepl("^truth_rows_", name), "True values",
    grepl("^sim_results_", name), "Simulated studies",
    grepl("^val_results_", name), "Independent check",
    default = NA_character_
  )]
  meta <- meta[!is.na(stage)]
  # Longest key first, so that "maringe" does not also match "maringe_exp"
  keys <- names(lab)[order(-nchar(names(lab)))]
  meta[, ds := vapply(name, function(n) {
    hit <- keys[vapply(keys, function(k) grepl(paste0("_", k, "(_[0-9a-f]+)?$"), n), logical(1))]
    if (length(hit)) hit[1] else NA_character_
  }, character(1))]
  rt <- dcast(meta[!is.na(ds), .(minutes = sum(seconds) / 60), by = .(stage, Model = lab[ds])],
              stage ~ Model, value.var = "minutes")
  knitr::kable(rt, digits = 1, col.names = c("Stage (CPU minutes)", names(rt)[-1]))
} else {
  cat("Run times are not available for this store.\n")
}
```
